articles.title: Sin pilotos y pocos controladores: ¿Qué puede fallar?
articles.raw_content: Normally, aviation is slow to embrace new technology—but AI has come for the skies.
articles.summary: La industria de la aviación, tradicionalmente lenta en adoptar nuevas tecnologías, se enfrenta ahora a la irrupción de la inteligencia artificial en el control de tráfico aéreo y la operación de aeronaves. Con la reducción de pilotos y controladores, se plantean riesgos operativos y de seguridad que requieren regulaciones y supervisión.

articles.title: Alerta científica: el umbral de 1,5 °C de cambio climático podría alcanzarse en 2029,
articles.raw_content:
ANTALYA, Turkey—Amid upbeat green-tech pep talks and notices for happy hours at the annual United Nations COP31 climate change conference on Thursday, two new reports offered a stark reminder of how far the world remains from containing global warming.

Climate Action Tracker, a nonprofit group that analyzes climate policies, found that the planet is still on track to warm nearly 5 degrees Fahrenheit by 2100, a rise that would devastate coral reefs, disrupt agriculture and forests and melt most of the world’s ice. In a separate bulletin, the European Union’s Copernicusclimate change service reported that global warming has accelerated significantly since the 2015 Paris climate agreement.

When the Paris agreement was adopted, the average global temperature was projected to surpass the pact’s long-term threshold of 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit above the preindustrial average around 2045. After another decade of global climate summits, warming is now projected to cross that benchmark as soon as 2029, according to Copernicus.

articles.summary: En la COP31, dos informes revelan que el planeta sigue en camino de subir casi 5 °F (≈2,8 °C) para 2100, superando el umbral de 1,5 °C antes de 2029. El servicio Copernicus de la UE confirma la aceleración del calentamiento, lo que amenaza infraestructuras, agricultura y ecosistemas europeos.

articles.title: Google lanza gafas inteligentes con enfoque en privacidad, precios desde 395 USD
articles.raw_content:
Smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days. Now, Google is ready to take another swing at "intelligent eyewear" for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they're no impulse buy.

These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered.

Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn't told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea.

Read full article

Comments
articles.summary: Google presenta gafas inteligentes impulsadas por Gemini, con énfasis en privacidad tras polémicas anteriores. La colaboración incluye a Samsung y diseñadores Gentle Monster y Warby Parker. Los modelos, disponibles en EE. UU. y Corea del Sur, empiezan en 395 USD, con opciones de montura y lentes variadas.

articles.title: Niña de 13 años pregunta a IA sobre suicidio en portátil escolar sin detección
articles.raw_content: The young girl’s parents allege that she used Gemini via her school Chromebook to plan her suicide, but the school’s monitoring systems didn’t know until it was almost too late.
articles.summary: Una niña de 13 años usó el modelo Gemini en el Chromebook escolar para planificar un suicidio. Sus padres denuncian que el sistema de supervisión de la escuela no detectó la actividad durante semanas, lo que provocó una alarma tardía. El caso destaca la necesidad de mejorar la detección de contenido sensible en dispositivos educativos.

articles.title: El CEO de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, enfrenta acusaciones de relación con posible espía china

As espionage targets go, Jensen Huang is perhaps one of the least surprising on Earth. The Nvidia CEO runs one of the world's most valuable companies, controls the in-demand technology fueling the AI boom, and is cozy with presidents, CEOs, and all manner of important people. He also wears a cool leather jacket.

Which makes Huang's admission that he had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy - reportedly while her spying was known to US intelligence and even President Donald Trump - all the more shocking. The fallout goes well beyond his marriage, his reputation, or Nvidia itself. Experts tell The Verge the incident threate …

articles.summary: El director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, ha sido acusado de haber mantenido una relación con una mujer sospechosa de ser espía china, a pesar de que la inteligencia estadounidense ya la conocía. El caso, que involucra a altos cargos y a la administración Trump, plantea riesgos de seguridad para la industria de IA y la reputación de Nvidia.

articles.title: Nvidia enfrenta crisis tras la investigación a Jensen Huang
articles.raw_content:
The investigation of Jensen Huang by Nvidia’s board threatens the future of one of Silicon Valley’s longest-serving executives and a key enabler of the AI boom, who has no obvious successor as leader of the world’s second-most-valuable company.

Huang is fighting for survival after admitting to an extramarital affair, believed to be with an executive at a large Nvidia customer whom US officials also allege was working as a Chinese spy.

The prospect that Huang could be forced out as chief executive of the US chipmaker he co-founded more than 30 years ago has alarmed investors and allies in the tech industry. Shares in Nvidia, which late last month ceded its position as the world’s most valuable to Apple amid a broader sell-off in AI stocks, had fallen more than 5 percent by midday trading on Monday.

Comments
articles.summary: El consejo de Nvidia está investigando a su CEO, Jensen Huang, por una relación extramarital con una ejecutiva que supuestamente trabajaba como espía chino. La posible salida de Huang preocupa a inversores y a la industria tecnológica, provocando una caída de más del 5 % en las acciones de la compañía. No hay sucesor claro.

As Reuters notes, the Anthropic IPO was previously expected to be valued at as much as $2 trillion. As of last week, Anthropic's rival OpenAI was valued at $1.25 trillion.

articles.title: El CEO de Nvidia admite su aventura y se convierte en problema de seguridad
articles.raw_content:
Nvidia’s chief executive Jensen Huang has admitted having an affair two days after the FT reported his alleged romantic relationship with a woman the US intelligence community believes was working as a spy for China.

Huang revealed the affair in an internal message to employees on Sunday that was obtained by the FT.

“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang said in the message. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
